subject: Re: Waveform Annotation Needs - Axoft
text:
Hi Santosh,

Really sorry it's taken me a while to come back to you on this. Waveform
annotation is something we're still in the middle of rolling out, but
here's how we'd approach the questions you raised.

The signals you listed - impedance, continuity, noise, leakage current,
stimulation response, electrode and channel performance - all come in as a
CSV. Each column shows up as its own channel on the timeline in the label
editor, so you can see the different signals charted together and label
across them.

For the labelling, you set up a time range label in your ontology and
annotators use it to mark events, anomalies or segments on the timeline.
That handles your third point nicely - drift, spikes, dropouts, saturation
and unstable baselines all get flagged as the range where they happen.

The other parts of your list are things I'm still waiting to confirm as
this moves into production. Pass/fail down to a single channel or
electrode, the finer labels like thresholds and response latency, and the
cross-modal one where an image defect links to an electrical reading in the
same task all sit in that group, so I'd rather nail those down before
putting them in writing. We do support multimodal annotation, which is what
the cross-modal workflow would build on, and that's the piece I most want
to get you a firm answer on.

So the short version is that annotating waveforms and flagging anomalies is
nearly there. The multimodal QC side is the more useful one for you.

If you can give me a rough picture of how their image and electrical data
are set up at the moment, I'll take the open questions back to the product
team and get you a proper answer on each.

Best,
Tom
